highlights.title: OpenAI says its Jalapeño chip can power faster AI responses than the competition
highlights.summary: OpenAI says its new AI chip, Jalapeño, completes tasks more efficiently and returns responses faster than other AI systems, according to a blog post published on Tuesday.
body: First introduced in June, Jalapeño is an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) made in partnership with Broadcom. It’s designed for AI inference — the process of running a trained AI model to complete a task or deploy an agent.

To measure Jalapeño’s performance, OpenAI used InferenceX, a benchmarking platform that shows how well AI systems handle inference. The test compared Jalapeño’s performance against the best results recorded at the time, which were with Nvidia’s GB200 or GB300 superchips. OpenAI says Jalapeño delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1, and Kimi K2.5 1T than the comparison systems, while offering 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency across the three models. That means the chip can provide users with “faster responses, more responsive agents, and more reliable access as the demand grows,” according to Ho.

OpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño in “small volumes” by the end of this year, but will begin to “ramp the volume up” into 2027, Ho added. The company doesn’t say how many chips it plans to deploy next year, however.

highlights.summary: Julian Alvarez must take one of two paths before the transfer deadline: stay at Atletico Madrid and try to rebuild his connection with the fans or get his head around a potential move to Arsenal.
body: Atletico have told him again that they will not sell him to Barcelona and that - coupled with the reaction of the club's supporters on Sunday - has left him "devastated", according to well-placed sources in Spain.
The situation is now "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," he told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

highlights.title: Paradox's latest grand strategy Afterworld wants you to survive the post-apocalypse
highlights.summary: After a succession of grand strategy sequels - including Crusader Kings 3, Victoria 4, and Europa Universalis 5 - Paradox has unveiled Afterworld, its first grand strategy game to feature an original setting in over a decade.
body: As its name hints at, Afterworld whisks strategy fans to a post-apocalyptic future; specifically a post-apocalyptic North America blighted with hazardous terrain, dangerous old-world ruins, and the desperate remnants of humanity. Through this hostile, procedurally generated landscape, players must slowly grow a small group of survivors into a continent-spanning empire - by first scavenging food, water, and shelter, before rediscovering the basic methods of civilisation and expanding from there.

Paradox describes Afterworld as a "story rich" strategy game, which begins with players choosing one of several origin stories for their group - perhaps they've been forced to abandon a failed nuclear bunker, or are "wayward zealots looking for their goddess in the dustlands". Then as the group grows, they'll learn new skills and rediscover technologies (all unlocked dynamically based on what players find as they explore), set up convoys and supply lines, encounter rival groups, negotiate trades,and fight where necessary.

highlights.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
highlights.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: My pup Koopa and I put 15 dog beds to the test – these are ones that survived
highlights.summary: We tried models from Black Lab, K9 Ballistics, Orvis, Znooz and others to find beds that were long-lasting, washable, and most of all, comfortable. The best dog harnesses and dog toys – pup-tested. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: While our four-legged best friends are often happy enough to sprawl on the floor or curl up on an old blanket, there’s an increasing number of companies out there making plush and durable spots for pampered pups to lie.

But given the destructive tendencies of some dogs and that some of these beds cost well into the hundreds of dollars, buying the wrong one can quickly turn into an expensive mess. We tested 15 different models to find the best for every situation.

I’ve tested everything from sports cars to smartphones for dozens of international outlets since the late 90s, but I’ve been a dog owner and lover my entire life. For the Filter, my pups and I have put dog harnesses and dog toys to the test. Along the way, my pups have curled up on everything from leftover couch cushions to high-grade beds from big-brand stores.
I’ve seen which types of beds work and which fall apart, which are easy to take apart and which are a real struggle and which stand up best to repeated cleaning and drying cycles.

highlights.title: Claude Cowork finally remembers what you told the app in chat
highlights.summary: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.
body: A change to Claude’s memory system will eliminate one of the most annoying things about using agents — the constant need to rebrief the AI on things it already knows. On Tuesday, Anthropic announced it’s merging the memory system used by chat and Claude Cowork, which means that Claude will always remember what it learned in one area, even when you’re engaging with it in another.
Anthropic is also exposing what Claude has retained in its memory, allowing users to read, edit, or delete information on any topic.
The update will improve the experience for Claude’s users as it will allow them to more seamlessly move between the research phase and taking action.

Before, you may have developed ideas for projects over time while chatting with Claude, but when it came time to actually enact the changes, you’d have to start over by telling Cowork all the details. This was incredibly frustrating. The update makes Claude now feel like one continuous assistant, rather than two separate products under one roof.
points: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.

highlights.title: Taiwan charges nine people for smuggling ‘high-end’ AI servers to China
highlights.summary: Among those charged are two Super Micro employees and one from Nvidia, marking another flashpoint in US-China AI rivalry. Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people Monday, including one from Nvidia and two from Super Micro, for illegally exporting “high-end AI servers” to mainland China, adding…
body: Prosecutors said the servers involved were graphics processing units known as “B300,” which have been banned from sale to China.

Seventy-four servers arrived in China successfully, according to the prosecutors. Of those, 50 were sent through Indonesia, 16 delivered directly to China and eight sent to Japan first, then Hong Kong, before they landed in mainland China.
Another attempt involving 56 servers failed, and the servers remain in Taiwan, said the prosecutor’s office.

AI infrastructure, including advanced semiconductors mostly made in Taiwan, has become a key point of competition between the US and China. Washington began imposing restrictions on Nvidia’s exports of advanced chips to China in 2022 and tightened them in subsequent years. In April 2025, the US required licenses for exports of Nvidia’s H20 chips to China before allowing some sales to resume later that year.

body: Littler was beaten 6-5 by Jermaine Wattimena in a final-leg decider, with the Dutchman going on to take the title in Leicester, overcoming countryman Kevin Doets 8-6 in the final.
Littler beat Archie Self 6-2, Arno Merk 6-3 and then William O'Connor 6-3 to set up a last-16 tie with Chris Dobey, who he thrashed 6-0, before losing out to eventual champion Wattimena.
The world No 1 has won every major title on the PDC circuit so far in 2026 - the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

He still needs to win the World Series, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals this season in order to achieve something no-one has ever managed in the sport.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

“Leonard brought uncommon experience, intelligence, and perspective to every campaign and every conversation,” said longtime collaborator and president of Weissman/Markovitz Communications Rick Markovitz. “He was a skilled raconteur, and I will miss his passion for storytelling and hearing about the old days of Hollywood.”
Morpurgo’s vast experience and enduring presence made him well-known as an international film publicity professional.

highlights.title: People’s bodies are changing in the age of Ozempic. How are we meant to talk about it?
highlights.summary: Discussing people’s bodies can be fraught. We asked eating disorder experts how to do so – or not – responsibly. In the age of Ozempic and people being open about plastic surgery, discussion about people’s bodies is rife.
body: It is a fraught topic. We asked eating disorder experts for guidelines to follow when talking about other people’s bodies, and how to do so without doing harm.

For experts in the field of eating disorders, the current ambivalence makes sense. “There’s a whiplash moment we’re stuck in,” says Dr Tom Hildebrandt, director of the Center for Eating and Weight Disorders at Mount Sinai hospital in New York.

The body positivity movement of the 2010s saw a mainstream push to “accept all body sizes, shapes and types”, says Hildebrandt. Then, with the explosion of GLP-1s, progress toward body acceptance “took a hard right turn”, he says – once again, “the media went through its idealization of weight loss”.
The vocabulary is different than it was before. Now, the focus is on “optimizing” one’s body and appearance, says Dr Ulrike Schmidt, professor of eating disorders at King’s College London.

highlights.title: Preserving glow-in-the-dark art and fashion for future generations
highlights.summary: Fashionistas of a certain age no doubt remember the late designer Stephen Sprouse, who gave Blondie's Debbie Harry her distinctive Bowery punk style. Sprouse's first collections in the mid-1980s made a major splash, melding graffiti prints, a playful '60s aesthetic, and bright Day-Glo colors that…
body: Several examples of Sprouse's work are preserved in the textiles collection of the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields, where conservationists are trying to learn more about the phosphorescent and fluorescent pigments the designer used in his creations in order to keep the colors from dulling over time. They described recent advances in that research at a meeting of the American Chemical Society (ACS) held this week in Chicago.

Scientists began describing minerals that glowed in the dark as phosphors in the Middle Ages. Typically, such materials take on a charge when exposed to light, storing the absorbed energy and releasing it gradually as re-emitted light. Henri Becquerel discovered radioactive decay in 1896 because of his work with phosphorescent uranium salts: He left the salts in a closed drawer with photographic plates, which fogged up even without a light source. DayGlo paints and similar materials exploit the related phenomenon of fluorescence. DayGlo pigments fluoresce in daylight by essentially converting UV light into visible light to produce brighter, more vibrant colors.

highlights.title: Every Big Announcement from Gamescom Opening Night Live
highlights.summary: We might not have E3 anymore, but at least we have Gamescom. The Cologne, Germany-based gaming extravaganza is the summer's last must-see event before a busy fall season packed with new game releases.
body: From The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past to Tides of Annihilation, Gamescom Opening Night Live was packed with exciting announcements and trailers. Here’s a breakdown of the biggest games that were showcased.

CD Projekt Red closed the show with the upcoming The Witcher 3 expansion, which will be released in 2027 — a full 12 years after the base game came out. In its first trailer, we got an idea of Songs of the Past ’s story and a new chain weapon for Geralt. A developer joined host Geoff Keighley on stage and said Songs of the Past would be Geralt's "last adventure" before the series passes the torch to Ciri. The Witcher 4 wasn’t shown off, but at least we know CDPR is targeting a 2028 release window for Ciri’s new adventure.

The Witcher 3 is also getting a remaster with upgraded visuals, new finishers, expanded photo mode, new Signs FX, and so much more. It'll be a free upgrade for all The Witcher 3 owners on Sept. 29. Also, the previous expansions Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine will be made free for all players starting Tuesday.

highlights.title: I’ve been told to apply to a civil and administrative tribunal over my faulty dishwasher. What does it involve?
highlights.summary: Taking a consumer complaint to tribunal is likely to be onerous, writes policy professional Kat George, but the payoff may be worthwhile. A little over two years ago, I bought a new dishwasher. From the beginning, it did not function properly.
body: The retailer refused to accept a return for a refund or replacement, and because I bought it for my tenant, I had to replace it at my own cost. The whole process has been very frustrating, and I now have a useless dishwasher stored in my home, which remains under the manufacturer’s warranty.

I submitted a complaint to Fair Trading in a bid to force the retailer to engage with the issue, however the outcome was the same. Fair Trading says my next step is to apply to the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NCAT), if I am eligible. My question is: what would applying to NCAT involve? Could it lead to further costs for me?

Kat says: This is an extraordinarily frustrating situation. Under the Australian Consumer Law, however, you may have a strong argument that the dishwasher’s performance breaches the consumer guarantees.

highlights.title: Google's anti-nausea Motion Assist dots finally rolling out on Android
highlights.summary: Some people are cursed with motion sickness, which can make it impossible to read or use a phone in a moving vehicle without suffering waves of nausea. There's a surprisingly simple trick that can make smartphones usable in such situations.
body: Motion sickness is caused by a disagreement between what your inner ear senses and what your eyes see. If you're looking at a book or a screen while in a car, the sensory mismatch can lead to a pretty unpleasant time. As part of iOS 18 in 2024, Apple released a feature called Motion Cues that places a network of moving dots on the screen to alleviate motion sickness, and it seems to work surprisingly well. Google's version is similar, but it's called Motion Assist.

Google began testing Motion Assist back in 2024, but it never expanded beyond an internal test until now. Android Authority reports Motion Assist is appearing on Pixel phones running Android 17, but there's no app or update you can install to get the feature—it's being delivered by Play Services as part of a staged rollout.

highlights.title: It Should Be Harder to Apply for a Job. No, Really
highlights.summary: Thanks to a dwindling supply of open roles, “one-click” applications, and the rise of artificial intelligence, it’s easier than ever to apply for a job. We’re all paying the price.
body: Three years ago, Andrew Stockwell had his hiring routine down to a science.

As head of people for the software-buying company Vendr, Stockwell posted a listing, waited a few days, and then reviewed a few dozen applications—up to 100, if he was lucky. Recruiters identified other potential candidates, adding a few more applicants to the mix. Stockwell read résumés, conducted interviews, and passed along sterling candidates to hiring managers.
“It was really about finding that great talent, sussing out that talent, speaking with that talent, and identifying the best possible people,” Stockwell tells WIRED.

Stockwell is one of many recruitment professionals who believe looking for a job is fundamentally broken. In 2026, job hunting has become as easy as online shopping: AI can crank out tailored résumés and cover letters in seconds. Browser extensions can autofill applications, no human necessary. LinkedIn serves users dozens of jobs a day, many with the option to apply with “just a few clicks.”

body: Paxton, endorsed by Donald Trump but facing a close contest against Democrat James Talarico, posted a “Texas first” datacenter plan on X with a graphic that the social media network flagged as “Made with AI”.

Republicans have been struggling to keep up with a shift in public opinion fueled by concerns that power- and water-hungry datacenters will push up energy costs and harm the environment. Some fear the issue could prove costly in November’s US midterm elections.

An Annenberg Public Policy Center survey last month found that 61% of Americans now oppose the building of a new datacenter in their area, an increase from 49% in March. This includes 69% of Democrats, 54% of Republicans and 53% of independents.

Last year Greg Abbott, the governor of Texas, dubbed his state the “epicenter of AI development”, but on Sunday he told ABC’s This Week program that tech companies “basically dug their own grave for the problem that’s been caused for them and that’s why they got the backlash they deserve”.

highlights.title: OpenAI subpoenaed by Alabama AG over Hugging Face hack
highlights.summary: Alabama's attorney general issued a subpoena to OpenAI on Monday as part of an investigation into how one of its AI agents escaped a supposedly secure testing environment and autonomously hacked another company last month.
body: The state is investigating whether OpenAI’s ‘inability or unwillingness to ensure the safety of its products’ endangers citizens.
The investigation seeks to determine whether OpenAI’s safety practices violated state consumer protection laws and pose a risk to Alabama citizens, the AG’s office said in a statement.

“This AI lab leak showed that Alabamians’ and Americans’ worst fears about artificial intelligence are not just theoretical,” said Attorney General Steve Marshall. “Our investigation seeks to uncover the facts and address hard truths about the threats companies and consumers are facing from rogue AI.”

Marshall was among 15 red state attorneys general who wrote to OpenAI asking it to preserve records about the Hugging Face hack last month. The subpoena adds to mounting scrutiny over safety practices at frontier labs in the wake of both that incident and other episodes subsequently uncovered elsewhere, including Anthropic and Meta.

highlights.title: The Whimsical British Country-House Fantasy Is Taking Over Upstate New York
highlights.summary: Across the Hudson Valley and Catskills, hoteliers and designers are embracing chintz, antiques, and charming imperfections.
body: “Britain is a country of great eccentrics,” muses interior designer Adam Greco, whose own view of ‘British whimsy’ manifests in charming chintz and heirloom curios, filtered through the lens of cultural treasures like Sherlock Holmes and Mary Poppins. It's a highly romanticized spin, something the New York City–based designer, who's worked on properties like London's The Ned and Oslo's Sommerro, felt wanting in the hospitality space, even across many landmark British hotels. “As a foreigner I remember walking into a grand hotel on London’s Regent’s Street and thinking it looked like a function room in Cincinnati inside,” he says. “It was disappointing.”

Recently, though, a wave of UK properties have started to embrace the kinds of cultural eccentricities that Greco saw as lacking in those hotels. This updated approach to the whimsical British aesthetic, all vintage bric-a-brac set alongside some serious art collections and sumptuous fabrics, is best expressed in the UK at properties like the Three Horseshoes in Batcombe, about 20 miles south of Bath, and the Fort Road Hotel in Margate along the southeast coast.

highlights.title: Two unvaccinated people die from measles in Pennsylvania, officials confirm
highlights.summary: Two unvaccinated people have died from measles in Pennsylvania, state health officials confirmed Tuesday. They are the first measles deaths reported in Pennsylvania in 35 years and the first deaths reported in the US in 2026.
body: Citing privacy, health officials in Pennsylvania are not providing information on the people who died beyond that they were unvaccinated and were residents of Lancaster County. Officials noted that the deaths are among 393 confirmed cases reported this year across 28 counties in the state.

The new deaths come as vaccination rates continue to slip nationwide and cases of the virus—one of the most contagious in the world—continue to surge. Already in 2026, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has tallied at least 2,777 cases, the highest total since 1991.

The US had previously declared measles eliminated in 2000, after concerted vaccination efforts broke the chains of transmission over a 12-month period. But now, US vaccination rates have slipped to around 92 percent, significantly below the 95 percent target needed to prevent the virus from spreading in communities. Non-medical vaccination exemptions, meanwhile, have reached yet another record high this year, hitting 4 percent.

highlights.title: Spirit Airlines Wants to Sell Its Data to Google. Former Flight Attendants Are Freaked Out
highlights.summary: “It never crossed my mind that they would be so bold as to sell our private data for AI,” says one former Spirit Airlines flight attendant.
body: Spirit Airlines may have declared bankruptcy this spring, but the budget airline is still worth something—to AI giants, at least. In mid-August, Google won a $10 million bid to purchase some 34 years of the airline’s data, from invoices and flight operations information to Wi-Fi sales, employee records, and crew pairings.

In a statement, a Google spokesperson said the data “can be helpful in improving our products and AI models.” The sale would not include customer data, and Google “will not receive any personal information from this dataset,” the spokesperson said. The winning offer, chosen over a competing $7.5 million proposal from AI data and training company Mercor, has to be approved by a judge.
The employee data “has no business being sold,” Sara Nelson, the president of the AFA, said in a written statement to WIRED. “This is outrageous!”

highlights.summary: Guy Ritchie has spent decades bouncing between crime capers, spy thrillers, and blockbuster franchises, but one of the filmmaker's most acclaimed movies feels remarkably different from the projects that made him famous.
body: Guy Ritchie's The Covenant is one of the filmmaker's best-reviewed pictures, and it's now getting a new lease on life streaming on Hulu. In the picture, Jake Gyllenhaal stars as Sergeant John Kinley, an American soldier on a tour of duty in Afghanistan. Featuring local interpreters, the film draws on stories and plot threads largely inspired by true events.

What makes Guy Ritchie's The Covenant particularly interesting within his larger filmography is that it tends to abandon the filmmaker's usual bag of tricks. Those looking for Ritchie's typical fast-talking British gangsters or the heightened blockbuster antics seen in Sherlock Holmes won't find much of it here. Instead, Ritchie delivers a surprisingly straightforward war thriller built nearly entirely around the relationship between two men.

highlights.title: 9 Best Collagen Creams Work Overtime to Plump and Firm Skin
highlights.summary: Do collagen creams really work? Nine doctors weigh in, revealing everything you need to know about choosing a collagen cream for a more youthful complexion.
body: Here’s the juicy truth about anti-aging skincare: Prioritizing moisture can help the skin maintain a firm, bouncy appearance long after collagen levels start to decline. And the best collagen creams—which can moisturize, boost collagen production, and protect existing collagen—go a long way to make up for lost proteins.

To find the right collagen cream for your routine, consider your goals. “For a quick hydration boost, opt for formulas with collagen,” Valerie Aparovich, a biochemist, certified cosmetologist-aesthetician, and the science team lead at OnSkin, instructs. While hydration alone can plump and boost radiance, firming and wrinkle reduction call for ingredients—like peptides and exosomes—that can penetrate the surface of the skin to stimulate collagen production in the dermal layers. And when it comes to preserving existing collagen, antioxidants are key.

And with that key to collagen creams, you’re ready to shop! Ahead, find an edit of the best of them, whether you’re in the market for a buzzy K-beauty find, a high-tech formulation, or the Elemis cream that started it all.
